summary: Round 7. The round-6 major is fixed in the geometry. Probing the built body shows the arm nut seat at z 3.3 with 3.3 mm of plate under it, the nut top at z 5.7, and the M3 x 12 tips at z 6.0, 1 mm below the body top (z 7). route_check now tests every wire against every screw and has a unit test. The body FEA load sits on the new nut seat, with the hot spot at the arm_1 root (10.15 vs 11.67 MPa). Every other check passes. The new screw length broke the shopping list, though. No price entry exists for M3 x 12 or M2 x 12, so the BOM falls back to size-only entries whose buy links are 100-packs of M3 x 8 and M2 x 6. A builder who follows the links gets arm screws that cannot reach their nuts and VTX screws that cannot reach the bosses. That is a major finding, so the verdict is FAIL.

findings.issue: The BOM buy links are for the wrong screw lengths. bom.md row 'M3 x 12 mm socket head screw' (8 off, the arm screws) links to Zoro SC22030080, an 'M3 ... 8 mm L, 100 PK'. catalog/prices.json has no 'screw:M3x12:socket', so ship.py falls back to 'screw:M3:socket', which is an M3 x 8 pack (it was an exact M3 x 14 entry in round 6, so the M3 x 12 change caused this). The row 'M2 x 12 mm socket head screw' (4 off, VTX) has the same fault: it links to the M2 x 6 pack SC22020060. The row price is also taken from the wrong pack. An M3 x 8 from below with a 6 mm grip ends at z 2, short of the nut seat at z 3.3, so it engages nothing. An M2 x 6 cannot clamp the VTX through its 6 mm spacer. The ship.py docstring says the size fallback is 'from an assortment pack', but these entries are single-length packs. ('screw:M3:flat' even has an M2 button-head pack as its source.)
findings.fix: Add exact 'screw:M3x12:socket' and 'screw:M2x12:socket' entries to catalog/prices.json, each with a real, opened source URL for that length. Engine (general): when a BOM row is priced from a size-only fallback key, either make that key point at a real assortment, or print a note in the row ('link is an M3 x 8 pack; buy M3 x 12') and add a warning to the report, so a wrong length can never be bought silently. Fix the source of 'screw:M3:flat' while you are there.

findings.issue: Round-6 major, now resolved. The only remaining exposure: each arm nut now sits at the bottom of an open 1 mm deep hex well (about 5.8 mm across flats) on the phase-wire line, with the thread end 1 mm below the top face and 0.3 mm above the nut. Soft 18 AWG silicone pressed into the well by a tie or a crash could still reach the thread end, but only if it bends to a radius of about 4 mm. That is unlikely.
findings.fix: Optional: after the arms are torqued, put a dab of hot glue or RTV in each of the 8 wells, or a 25 mm strip of Kapton under each phase bundle. Add one line to the build notes.

findings.issue: Thread engagement in the sunk nut is near the minimum. The tip is only 0.3 mm past the nut top. The M3 x 12 length tolerance is +/-0.35 mm (js15) and the tip chamfer is about 0.5 mm, so a short screw fully engages only about 1.8-2.2 mm of the 2.4 mm nut. The thread-stripping strength is still well over 1 kN against the 144 N design load, so this is not a strength problem. But no thread shows past the nut, so a nylon-insert nut cannot be used and the joint relies on threadlocker.
findings.fix: Accept it, and keep the blue threadlocker on these 8. In the build notes, say to check that the screw end is flush with or past the top of the nut.

findings.issue: Carried, still open. The generated ASSEMBLY.md step 2 says only 'Drive 8 x M3 x 12'. It never says to drop the 8 arm nuts into their pockets, to tape the 4 downward-opening stack nuts, or to use threadlocker. It also still puts all soldering after the strap. DESIGN.md has the right order, but the builder follows ASSEMBLY.md.
findings.fix: Engine: emit 'press N nuts into <part> pockets (opens down: tape them)' before the step that drives their screws. Print bom_extra notes (threadlocker) at the matching step. Allow the electrical steps to come before a named mechanical step (here, before top_plate).

findings.issue: Carried. The BOM row still reads 'heat-shrink for AWG 12 joints, 20 mm pieces', against the 8-10 mm the wiring note asks for at the XT60 cups. The XT60 is still held rearward only by the cable tie's friction. The hold-when-unplugging note now reaches WIRING.md and ASSEMBLY.md, which closes that part of the round-6 finding.
findings.fix: Make the AWG 12 heat-shrink row 10 mm. Optional: add a 0.8-1 mm rear retaining lip on the XT60 cradle.

findings.issue: WIRING.md shows the camera supply at 4.988-4.99 V against the catalog's 5.0 V minimum ('sags'), because 28 AWG over 110 mm sits on the 5 V rail. In practice it is harmless, but the generated sheet shows the camera below its rated input.
findings.fix: Power the camera from the stack's 9 V pad (the Phoenix 2 accepts 5-36 V per the catalog, and the BEC is rated 3 A), or use 26 AWG for cam_5v. Either gets rid of the sag row.

findings.issue: DESIGN.md numbers are stale after this round. It says body FEA is 9.6 MPa, but report.json now gives 10.15 MPa (p99.9, limit 11.67) with the load on the sunk nut seat. The arm envelope is given as 102 x 32 x 12.5, but the part is 103 x 32 x 12.5. The XT60 still has no weight_g, and the CNHL lead and XING2 lead gauge and length are still not catalogued (carried).
findings.fix: Update the body FEA figure and the arm envelope. Add XT60 weight_g and the lead data to the catalog, each with a source.

findings.issue: Carried. The counterbore ceilings in the arms and top plate open on the bed face and print as mid-air rings. This is documented in DESIGN.md only.
findings.fix: Turn on hole bridging / a sacrificial layer in the slicer, or model a 0.2 mm sacrificial layer. Put the note in the 3MF/ASSEMBLY output.

findings.issue: Carried, and handled by the documented gate. The 74 % output cap gives a central estimate of 57.4 A, so the real full-pack peak may reach about 60-66 A against the XT60's 60 A, 1-minute rating.
findings.fix: Keep the Blackbox/OSD check (peak 60 A or less) before freestyle. If the peak is over, lower motor_output_limit by 1-2 % (twr 6.18 has about 3 % margin).

findings.issue: Carried. The single strap band sits 14.5 mm ahead of the pack centre, so the rear of the pack is held only by the anti-slip pad.
findings.fix: If the pack shifts in testing, add a second band at about x -36 or move the VTX back.

findings.issue: Carried. At 0 deg tilt the cheek tips, and at 35-40 deg the roof tongue's front corners, may show at the edges of the 155 deg image. Both are clear at the 25 deg home tilt.
findings.fix: Check with the camera fitted. Chamfer or round them if they show.

findings.issue: Carried. The first arm bending mode is about 165 Hz, in the gyro noise band. The PETG-CF arm sits under a motor base that can reach 70-80 C.
findings.fix: Hover test plus a Blackbox gyro-noise check before freestyle. Consider a 0.5-1 mm standoff ring under each motor.
